correctness.rationale: A uniform tree of Theta(a,b,c) deletes exactly two edges on distinct paths, giving W=ab+ac+bc equally likely deletion pairs. Each pair of distinct deletion indicators has strictly negative covariance. Vertex degree equals host degree minus incident deletions, so nonadjacent vertices have strictly negative covariance. Shared-edge diagonal terms produce the two displayed positive rational forms, and elementary expansions show equality only for all edges of (2,2,2) and the middle length-three edge of (2,2,3). Independently implemented brute-force connectivity enumeration checked all 216 ordered triples a,b,c∈{2,...,7}; all vertex-pair exact rational covariances satisfy edge iff covariance≥0. All-length result follows from algebra, not finite enumeration.
